quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight and choosing a good lane position help other drivers see you. Keep a safe distance from vehicles ahead so you can react to hazards. Do not rely on eye contact alone to be seen.

questions.question: If road conditions require a longer stopping distance, you should:

options.text: Ask someone else to ride your motorcycle.

questions.explanation: When stopping takes longer than normal, stay farther back from the vehicle ahead. Use at least a three-second following distance on slippery roads, when you cannot see ahead, or in heavy traffic.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and keep your motorcycle upright to maintain traction.

questions.question: When another vehicle is following you too closely, you should:

options.text: Let the other driver pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the other driver pass you.
questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Change lanes safely if you can and allow them ahead of you. Speeding up may make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the rear brake firmly while increasing front brake pressure gradually.

questions.explanation: Apply both brakes at the same time to stop quickly.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. Instead, hold the handlebars firmly, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and lean forward. Pull off the road as soon as you can.

questions.question: To work properly, an eye or face shield should have all of these features, except:
questions.explanation: Good eye protection must be scratch-free, resist impact, fasten securely, allow air flow, and fit over eyeglasses. It does not need to be airtight.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 and older, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means legal intoxication. It is illegal and unsafe to operate a motorcycle while intoxicated.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of being in a crash, you should:

options.text: Avoid using turn signals when changing lanes.
Watch only about five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: Reduce crash risk by staying visible, using your signals, and keeping a safe distance from other vehicles. Watch the road ahead, to the sides, and behind. Be prepared to avoid hazards at any time.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, you should:

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely so they can move.
Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
Use a lot of throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet so it doesn't cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
questions.explanation: Hold the handgrips firmly when riding over rough surfaces. This helps you keep control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals are how riders communicate in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: After entering a turn, you should roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through a turn to keep your suspension stable. Maintain a steady speed or speed up slowly as you go through the turn.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders who wear helmets.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Stay calm, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Move to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles may weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, but this is usually not dangerous. Stay calm and ride straight ahead at a steady speed. Weaving to match the movement will make it more dangerous.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway may not see you. What should you do to help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane. You don't have to help.
Move to another lane away from the ramp if you can.
Weave in your lane to be more visible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane away from the ramp if you can.
questions.explanation: Give merging drivers plenty of space to enter safely. Change lanes away from the ramp if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them room to merge.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, the best group formation is:
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when riding through curves, through turns, and when entering or leaving a highway. Staggered formation is best for straight roads.

questions.question: A passenger should never:

options.text: Lean with the operator when turning.

questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets. Passengers should lean with the operator during turns and avoid loose clothing that might catch on the motorcycle. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: One way to tell if your rear tire has gone flat while riding is if:

options.text: There is a hissing noise from the back.
The back end jerks from side to side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk side to side. You usually won't hear a tire fail while riding.

questions.question: The front brake supplies how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: At the rear of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This position allows experienced riders behind them to watch and help them.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator slow down?
questions.explanation: Downshifting is a way to slow down a motorcycle. Be aware that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to impair your riding ability?

options.text: Begins at about half of the legal limit.
Occurs only if you have had multiple drinks.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. You can be impaired before you reach the legal blood alcohol limit. Never drink any amount of alcohol before riding.

questions.question: What should you do when braking on a slippery surface?

options.text: Not use any brakes, but downshift.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes gently if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility to other drivers?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: To be more visible, keep your headlight on at all times. Also wear bright or reflective clothing and change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: Which item provides the best face protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not adequate protection.

questions.question: How does carrying a passenger or cargo affect your motorcycle?

options.text: It may take less time to accelerate, but more time to stop.
It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
It may take more time to accelerate, but less time to stop.
It may take less time to accelerate and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo slows down acceleration and stopping distance.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to ride directly alongside another vehicle?

options.text: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
Is better than riding behind the other vehicle.
Is safe because it limits your escape routes.
Should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can place you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle puts you in the driver's blind spot. The driver may not see you and could change lanes into you. You also lose your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What is NOT part of a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: A pre-ride inspection includes checking tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn. Do a complete pre-ride inspection before every ride.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever located on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is located on the left handgrip of a motorcycle.
